Executive Overview

This report analyzes 12,343 records spanning 21 years (2015–2035) across six countries and ten technology-centric job roles to examine how AI automation is reshaping the global job market. The dataset includes both historical observations (2015–2024) and simulated projections (2025–2035), enabling a forward-looking assessment of workforce risks and opportunities.

Five Critical Takeaways

  1. Automation risk is accelerating. The average AI risk score has risen from 0.30 in 2015 to a projected 0.51 in 2035 — a 72.0% increase. The sharpest acceleration occurs post-2030, suggesting the next decade will see disproportionate disruption.
  2. Salary growth is positive but uneven. Median salaries have grown 51.6% from 2015 to 2035, yet the gap between high-risk and low-risk roles is widening. Low-risk roles command a 57% salary premium over high-risk roles.
  3. Job survival is declining in the projection period. While 89.0% of all roles currently show survival prospects (class ≥1), the survival rate drops from 91.1% in 2015 to a projected 83.7% in 2035 — a concerning downward trajectory.
  4. Two roles face existential risk. Business Analysts (57.0% at-risk) and Data Analysts (43.5% at-risk) are the only roles with material at-risk populations. All other eight roles show survival rates above 97%.
  5. Skill demand is stable but shifting. Java and Python show the strongest demand growth through 2035, while traditional operational skills like Docker and Deep Learning are projected to see relative declines in demand scores.

AI Automation Risk Landscape

Understanding where automation risk concentrates is essential for prioritizing workforce investments. This section examines risk distributions across job titles, countries, and experience levels.

Risk by Job Title

The data reveals a stark bifurcation: two roles dominate the high-risk category, while the remaining eight cluster in low-to-medium risk territory.

Highest Risk: Business Analyst (avg risk score: 0.75) — 18.6% of all records fall into the High Risk category, driven largely by Business Analysts and Data Analysts.
Lowest Risk: AI Researcher (avg risk score: 0.15) — AI Researchers, Cybersecurity Analysts, and ML Engineers form a resilient cluster with risk scores below 0.26.

Risk by Geography

Country-level differences are modest but meaningful. India shows the highest average risk score (0.401), while the UK and Canada are marginally lower at 0.393. The narrow range (0.393–0.401) suggests that role selection matters more than geography for individual risk exposure.

Risk by Experience Level

Contrary to intuition, experience level shows minimal correlation with AI risk. Entry-level roles average 0.396, Mid-level 0.399, and Senior 0.393. However, survival rates improve significantly with seniority — from 83.9% (Entry) to 94.5% (Senior) — suggesting that while automation risk is role-dependent, senior professionals have greater adaptability.

Salary Trends & Segmentation

Compensation dynamics reveal both opportunity and vulnerability. This section tracks salary evolution across dimensions and explicitly examines the critical relationship between pay and automation risk.

Salary by Country

The USA commands a significant salary premium with a median of $43,422 — more than 3× India's median of $12,448. This gap persists across all roles and experience levels, reflecting both market size and currency effects.

Salary by Job Title & Experience

AI Researcher leads compensation at $42,845 median, followed by ML Engineers at $39,327. At the bottom, Data Analyst roles median $18,692 — a gap directly correlated with their higher automation risk.

Experience level shows the strongest salary differentiation: Senior roles median $48,318, Mid-level $32,996, and Entry $22,924 — a 2.1× spread from Entry to Senior.

The Salary × Automation Risk Correlation

This report's highest-value insight: salary and AI risk are negatively correlated (r = -0.245). Roles with higher automation risk systematically earn less.

Key Finding: Low-risk roles (median $34,105) earn a 57% premium over high-risk roles (median $21,683). This premium is not merely a coincidence — it reflects market pricing for scarcity, specialized expertise, and strategic value. High-risk roles tend to involve repetitive analytical or administrative tasks that AI can replicate, while low-risk roles require creative judgment, security expertise, or deep technical specialization.

Salary Bucket Distribution

Nearly 78% of all records fall into the "High" salary bucket, reflecting the technology-sector skew of the dataset. Only 5.2% are classified as "Low." However, within the high-risk roles (Business Analyst, Data Analyst), the Low and Medium salary buckets are overrepresented.

Skill Demand Trends (2015–2035)

Looking at growth trajectories, Java shows the strongest projected demand growth at 5.1%, followed by Python at 3.7% and AWS at 3.5%. Conversely, Docker (-3.2%) and Deep Learning (-1.5%) are projected to see relative declines.

Paradox Alert: Deep Learning has the lowest AI risk (0.15) and 100% survival rate, yet its skill demand is projected to decline slightly. This suggests the field may be maturing — demand stabilizing as supply catches up — rather than losing strategic importance.

Skill Demand vs. AI Risk

The scatter plot below reveals two distinct clusters: high-demand, low-risk skills (Python, Security, Docker, Deep Learning) and high-demand, high-risk skills (Excel, SQL). The strategic implication is clear — professionals should prioritize skills in the lower-left quadrant.

Job Survival & Market Outlook

Job survival classification (0 = at risk, 1 = moderate, 2 = strong) provides a forward-looking lens on workforce resilience. Combined with job opening trends, it reveals where labor demand is expanding and contracting.

Survival by Job Title

The survival distribution is heavily polarized. AI Researcher, DevOps Engineer, ML Engineer, and Cybersecurity Analyst all show 100% survival rates (no at-risk records). At the opposite extreme, Business Analyst shows only a 43.0% survival rate, with 57.0% of records classified as at-risk.

Survival by Country & Education

Geography matters: the USA offers the strongest survival prospects (93.8%), while India lags at 78.6%. Education level, surprisingly, shows minimal impact — Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD holders have nearly identical at-risk proportions (10.3%–11.9%). This suggests that role and skill choices outweigh formal education as survival factors in the AI era.

Job Openings Trends

Labor demand is shifting toward security and strategy roles. Cybersecurity Analyst leads opening growth at 49.1% (2015→2035), followed by Product Manager at 45.4%. Conversely, DevOps Engineer openings are projected to contract by 27.8%, and Data Scientist openings by 13.3%.

Market Signal: The fastest-growing opening categories (Cybersecurity, Product Management) align with the lowest-risk roles, while contracting categories (DevOps, Data Scientist) are in the low-to-medium risk zone. This suggests the market is already pricing in AI's differential impact.

Fastest-Growing AI Risk

While absolute risk levels matter, risk velocity — how fast risk is increasing — is equally important for workforce planning. AI Researcher shows the steepest risk acceleration at 400% growth from 2015 to 2035, followed by Cybersecurity Analyst at 133% and ML Engineer at 133%.

Important Context: These high percentage growth figures reflect low starting bases. AI Researchers began at 0.05 risk in 2015 and are projected to reach 0.25 in 2035 — still well within the "Low Risk" category. The absolute risk levels for these roles remain manageable.

Best Survival Combinations

The data identifies specific role-country-education combinations with perfect (100%) survival rates. The top combination is Software Engineer in USA with PhD. Other perfect-survival combinations include AI Researcher roles across all major countries and Software Engineering roles in North America and Europe with any education level.

Strategic Recommendations

Every recommendation below is grounded in a specific data finding from this analysis. No generic advice — only data-driven action.

1

Immediate: Redeploy Business Analyst & Data Analyst Talent

Data basis: Business Analysts show 57.0% at-risk classification and Data Analysts 43.5% — the only two roles with material at-risk populations. Their average AI risk scores (0.75 and 0.65) are 2× the dataset average.

Action: Launch targeted reskilling programs moving these populations toward SQL/Python-based analytics engineering, cybersecurity fundamentals, or product management tracks. The 46.9% salary gap between high-risk and low-risk roles provides a clear ROI case for reskilling investment.

2

Near-Term: Invest in Cybersecurity & AI Research Pipelines

Data basis: Cybersecurity Analyst job openings are projected to grow 49.1% through 2035 — the fastest of any role. AI Researchers command the highest median salary ($42,845) and maintain 100% survival with 88.9% "strong" survival classification.

Action: Expand university partnerships, apprenticeship programs, and internal rotation pathways into these functions. Prioritize recruitment in the USA and UK, where salary premiums and survival rates are highest.

3

Ongoing: Shift Skill Development from Excel to Python/Java

Data basis: Excel-associated roles (Business Analyst) have 0.75 average AI risk and 57.0% at-risk rate. Python and Java show the strongest demand growth (3.7% and 5.1% respectively) and are tied to roles with 99.9% and 97.4% survival rates.

Action: Mandate Python proficiency for all analytical roles by 2027. Replace Excel-centric training budgets with coding bootcamps and cloud certification programs (AWS demand growing 3.5%).

4

Structural: Address the India Survival Gap

Data basis: India shows the lowest survival rate (78.6%) and highest at-risk proportion (21.4%) of any country — more than 3× the USA's at-risk rate. This is driven by a higher concentration of Business Analyst and Data Analyst roles.

Action: In Indian operations, fast-track the transition from traditional BA/DA roles to engineering-centric profiles. Consider geographic arbitrage: move high-risk, low-margin work to lower-cost markets while building premium engineering capabilities in India.

5

Forward-Looking: Monitor Risk Velocity, Not Just Risk Level

Data basis: AI Researcher risk is growing at 400% from a low base, and Cybersecurity Analyst risk at 133%. While absolute levels remain safe, acceleration signals potential future disruption.

Action: Establish a quarterly "Automation Risk Dashboard" tracking year-over-year risk score changes by role. Set intervention triggers at 15% annual risk growth for any role, regardless of current absolute risk level.

6

Talent Strategy: Prioritize Experience Over Education for Risk Mitigation

Data basis: Education level has minimal impact on survival (10.3%–11.9% at-risk across all levels), while experience level shows a 10.6 percentage-point survival improvement from Entry (83.9%) to Senior (94.5%).

Action: Rebalance hiring budgets toward experienced professionals in high-risk roles. For entry-level hiring in at-risk functions, pair recruitment with structured 18-month rotation programs into lower-risk technical tracks.
